html:
The dissolution of Czechoslovakia took effect on 1 January 1993, when the federation split peacefully into the Czech Republic and Slovakia, each an independent state.

After the Velvet Revolution the two halves disagreed over how fast to reform the economy and how much power Slovakia should have. The 1992 elections were won by Václav Klaus in the Czech lands and Vladimír Mečiar in Slovakia, who agreed to part. No referendum was held, and polls showed most citizens wanted to stay together. The split went smoothly, unlike the breakup of Yugoslavia. Both states joined NATO and the European Union in 2004, and Slovakia adopted the euro in 2009.
sum: The dissolution of Czechoslovakia took effect on 1 January 1993, when the federation split peacefully into the Czech Republic and Slovakia, each an independent state.
